abstract_sentences.text: Despite improvements by length extrapolation, efficient attention and memory modules, handling infinitely long documents without performance degradation during extrapolation remains the ultimate challenge in long-text processing.

evidence.anchor: handling infinitely long documents without performance degradation

abstract_sentences.text: To solve this problem, we introduce a novel agent workflow, MEMAGENT, which processes text in segments and updates memory through an overwrite strategy, addressing the challenge of long-context task through enhanced memory management.

evidence.anchor: processes text in segments and updates memory through an overwrite strategy

abstract_sentences.text: We further extend the DAPO algorithm to directly optimize memory ability in an end-to-end fashion, facilitating training via independent-context multi-conversation generation.

Experimental results demonstrate that MEMAGENT has superb long-context capabilities, being able to extrapolate from an 8K context to a 3.5M QA task with a performance loss of less than 10% and achieving over 95% on the 512K NIAH test.

introduction_moves.previous_question: LLMs can perform complex tasks, but the paper has not scoped the long-context problem.
introduction_moves.current_answer: Books, long reasoning chains and agent memory overflow ordinary context windows.

evidence.anchor: how to handle long contexts effectively

introduction_moves.previous_question: Why does an ordinary context window fail in deployed tasks?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Overflowing text creates a capacity and processing bottleneck.

introduction_moves.previous_question: Can extrapolation, sparse/linear attention or compression solve the bottleneck alone?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Each family carries degradation, quadratic cost, retraining, hand-designed patterns or compatibility/parallelization costs.
introduction_moves.next_hook: State the trinity of desired properties.

evidence.anchor: Existing approaches to long-context tasks are three-pronged

introduction_moves.previous_question: What principle could satisfy all three properties?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Human note-taking keeps revealing concepts and discards redundant information.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Turn selective abstraction into a memory state.

evidence.anchor: we tend to abstract out the main revealing conceptions

introduction_moves.previous_question: How is selective abstraction implemented in an LLM?
introduction_moves.current_answer: A dynamically updated fixed-length memory is overwritten as chunks are read.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Explain how to train the read-write behavior.

introduction_moves.previous_question: How can multiple memory updates receive credit from a final answer?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Each context-independent conversation is treated as an optimization objective and shares the sample outcome.

evidence.anchor: treats each context-independent conversation as an optimization objective

introduction_moves.previous_question: What training algorithm implements the independent-context objective?
introduction_moves.current_answer: Multi-Conv DAPO extends DAPO with verifiable outcome reward.

introduction_moves.previous_question: Does the proposed memory work beyond the training length?
introduction_moves.current_answer: An 8K window trained on 60K-length documents is reported to answer QA up to 3.5M tokens.

introduction_moves.previous_question: What concrete contributions follow from the preview?
introduction_moves.current_answer: The first two bullets state arbitrary-length/linear inference and the workflow plus end-to-end Multi-Conv DAPO training.
The third bullet claims minimal degradation in RL-trained extrapolation.

method_moves.description: At each step the model sees the next chunk and a compact fixed-length memory.

evidence.anchor: the next chunk of text and a compact, fixed-length memory

method_moves.description: Memory overwrite is cast as retaining useful facts and discarding distractors for a later reward.

evidence.anchor: rewarded for retaining information and for discarding distractors

method_moves.description: Context-Processing repeatedly updates memory; Answer-Generation uses problem and memory to produce the final boxed answer.
Constant memory yields constant per-chunk cost and leaves the base tokenizer/attention layout unchanged.
RLVR and DAPO are used so one sample can generate several context-independent conversations.
Group, conversation and token indices separate the final answer from preceding writes.

evidence.anchor: The advantage value is derived from the conversation that contains the final answer

method_moves.description: Eq. (1) defines group-centered advantage; Eq. (2) defines token-normalized clipped DAPO with KL.

evidence.anchor: we do not devide the advantage by the standard deviation

method_moves.description: Eq. (3) defines a binary rule-based answer-equivalence reward.
Eq. (4) introduces latent memories and decomposes autoregressive likelihood into read/write factors.

evidence.anchor: Introducing the latent sequence m1:K−1 decomposes the original likelihood

method_moves.description: The MDP view unifies a reward-maximizing memory trajectory with long-text modeling.

evidence.anchor: learning an optimal distribution over memory states

experimental_design.name: research_question
experimental_design.description: The main question is whether an 8K bounded workflow extrapolates to long QA; §3.3.3 separately probes overwrite and lost-in-the-middle positions.

evidence.anchor: Our hypothesis is that overcoming such problem is a natural result of end-to-end optimization

experimental_design.name: backbone_and_framework
experimental_design.description: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct are used as backbones; multi-conversation training is based on verl.

experimental_design.name: curriculum
experimental_design.description: Stage I learns fundamental memory capabilities; Stage II transfers them to diverse contexts and difficult tasks, with the switch after roughly 400 steps.

evidence.anchor: stage I are fully converged, which takes about 400 steps

experimental_design.name: window_budget
experimental_design.description: The 8K budget is query 1024, context chunk 5000, memory 1024 and output 1024, with remaining tokens for the chat template.

evidence.anchor: This 8K window is allocated as follows

experimental_design.name: stage_I_data
experimental_design.description: 32,768 synthetic QA instances are built from HotpotQA-style golden paragraphs and distractors; 80,000 training samples are filtered and roughly half removed because a no-context Best-Of-2 score is 100%.

evidence.anchor: approximately 50% of the data are filtered out

experimental_design.name: stage_II_data
experimental_design.description: 2,560 instances with maximum length 60K combine DocQA-RL-1.6K with Stage I data.

evidence.anchor: 2,560 training instances with a maximum length of 60K tokens

experimental_design.name: extrapolation_test_sets
experimental_design.description: Synthetic tests use 50 to 6400 wiki items, corresponding to approximately 7K to 3.5M tokens.

evidence.anchor: wiki items ranges from 50 up to 6400

experimental_design.name: benchmarks
experimental_design.description: RULER-HQA, LongBench-QA, NIAH levels 1–3 and LongBench-SUM GovReport/QMSum cover moderate-density QA, high-density QA, low-density retrieval and summary.

evidence.anchor: We conduct comprehensive evaluations on several long-text benchmarks

experimental_design.name: baselines
experimental_design.description: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen, Qwen2.5-Instruct-1M, Qwen2.5-Instruct and QwenLong-L1 are main baselines; RAG and Mem0 are added in Appendix D.2.

experimental_design.name: metrics_and_scoring
experimental_design.description: Accuracy is used for QA/NIAH; summary uses ROUGE-1/2/L recall. Answers are regex-extracted, normalized and scored with sub-em; multi-part answers use the proportion of correct parts.

evidence.anchor: We employ the sub em score for all benchmarks

experimental_design.name: generation_controls
experimental_design.description: Baseline context and input/output generation lengths are listed in Table 6; MemAgent uses the fixed workflow budget.

experimental_design.name: random_seeds

experimental_design.description: Appendix A.3 gives KL 1×10^-3, no entropy loss, AdamW, learning rate 1×10^-6, warm-up 20, rollout batch 256, group 16 and off-policy ratio 16.

evidence.anchor: KL factor of 1 × 10−3 and disabling the entropy loss

result_inventory.claim: RL-MemAgent preserves RULER-HQA accuracy over much longer inputs than listed baselines.
result_inventory.value: 14B: 80.47 at 7K to 71.09 at 3.5M; 7B: 81.25 to 71.88. QwenLong-L1-32B falls from 72.66 at 7K to 11.72 at 896K; Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B-1M is 0.00 at 896K and N/A thereafter.
result_inventory.comparison: MemAgent is the only listed model with values at 1.75M and 3.5M; baselines degrade or become N/A earlier.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Accuracy point estimates per context length; no seed-level uncertainty or significance test. Figure 1 is a trend line.

evidence.anchor: Main experimental results comparing model performance across various context lengths
extend the evaluation to ultra-long contexts of 1.75M and 3.5M

result_inventory.claim: MemAgent has the highest or near-highest average among the listed LongBench-QA baselines at its corresponding scale.
result_inventory.value: MemAgent-14B AVG 51.0 versus QwenLong-L1-32B 50.7 and DS-Distill-Qwen-32B 49.0; MemAgent-7B AVG 48.2 versus Qwen2.5-Instruct-7B 34.7 and Qwen2.5-Instruct-7B-1M 39.5, but below DS-Distill-Qwen-32B 49.0.
result_inventory.comparison: Five-task averages and per-dataset accuracy compare QA generalization, not only retrieval length.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Arithmetic AVG of five accuracy columns; no variance, sample counts or significance test.

evidence.anchor: memory capabilities acquired through reinforcement learning are generalizable

result_inventory.claim: RL-MemAgent remains highly accurate on the synthetic NIAH retrieval stress test through 512K.
result_inventory.value: NIAH average at 512K is 98.18 for 14B and 96.62 for 7B; the 14B level values are 94.53/95.31/100.00 and 7B values are 92.97/96.88/96.88.
result_inventory.comparison: Most baselines drop at 128K–512K, while RL-MemAgent average loss from 8K to 512K is 1.56 points (14B) or 3.38 points (7B).
result_inventory.statistical_method: Heatmap accuracy over context-length × NIAH-level cells; no error bars.

evidence.anchor: Performance heatmaps on NIAH benchmark across different context lengths

result_inventory.claim: The learned memory policy transfers beyond QA to LongBench-SUM.
result_inventory.value: 14B GovReport ROUGE-1/2/L 37.16/12.03/16.23, AVG 21.80; QMSum AVG 31.39. 7B averages are 19.34 and 31.27.
result_inventory.comparison: 14B exceeds the best listed QMSum baseline AVG 29.84 and the listed GovReport averages near 19.34.
result_inventory.statistical_method: ROUGE recall point estimates and arithmetic AVG across ROUGE-1/2/L; no uncertainty.

evidence.anchor: learned general memory and context management capabilities

result_inventory.claim: The context-distribution probe shows no catastrophic position pattern in the tested synthetic setup.
result_inventory.comparison: The rows are differences from a random baseline rather than absolute scores; only two key-information groups and distractors are tested.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Accuracy differences at seven context lengths plus a reported AVG; no uncertainty.

evidence.anchor: other rows show the performance difference relative to random
remains consistently robust across all patterns

result_inventory.claim: The complexity argument predicts linear total FLOPs for fixed-window MemAgent versus quadratic baseline processing.
result_inventory.value: Appendix B Figure 10 estimates both methods over 8K–4M with q=1024, o=1024, N=5000; the text labels baseline O(n²) and MemAgent O(n).
result_inventory.comparison: MemAgent pays a fixed per-chunk window cost and grows in the number of chunks; the baseline processes the full context.
result_inventory.statistical_method: FLOP estimator, not a hardware runtime or throughput measurement.

evidence.anchor: baseline model exhibits an O(n2) complexity, while M EM AGENT achieves an O(n) complexity

result_inventory.claim: Removing RL destroys the long-context robustness that appears in the direct MemAgent workflow.
result_inventory.value: Figure 6 shows no-RL curves falling with length; Figure 7 shows only marginal or negative LongBench-QA changes without RL, while RL variants improve both settings.
result_inventory.comparison: Backbone and no-RL MemAgent are compared with RL-MemAgent at 7B/14B.

evidence.anchor: directly applying M EM AGENT leads to only marginal or even negative improvements

final_judgment.single_storyline: Fixed-length chunk-wise memory overwrite converts an unbounded document into a linear read-write trajectory; Multi-Conv DAPO uses final verifiable QA reward to shape each memory write.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the 8K budget, workflow/training diagrams, Eq. (1)-(4), baseline tables, length curves, cross-task results and RL/capacity/position ablations.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A-F move prompts, pseudocode, hyperparameters, data synthesis, scoring normalization, FLOP estimation, RAG/Mem0 comparisons, a positive case and failure trajectories; this improves recipe detail but leaves hardware, seeds and failure denominators absent.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figures 2-4 make the state transition and optimization structure visible; Table 1/Figure 5 align performance with context length; Figures 6-9 vary mechanism components rather than only adding baselines.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The O(N)/arbitrary-length narrative exceeds direct tests; Eq. (2) and Algorithm 1 show different optimization granularity; no explicit limitations or uncertainty are reported; Table 4's 14B AVG is not reproducible from its visible cells.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: A finite-window long-context paper should pair its fixed budget with cross-length results, component removal, runtime measurement and failure trajectories, and make pseudocode and objective use the same optimization granularity.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits stateful compression and agent-workflow papers; a purely theoretical complexity paper need not add benchmark failures, but must still separate assumptions, bound and empirical scope.
final_judgment.evidence_basis: Pages 3-10 establish the mechanism and main evidence; pages 17-29 provide implementation, complexity, comparison and failure boundaries.
